Subject: RE: Checkout assistant latency + streaming errors (urgent)

Quick triage notes (runtime / parser team):

What I see from the logs Tom sent:
- Multiple connection resets from our ingress with errors that map to parser state-machine failures.
- The client (redwood-js v2.3.1) started emitting an extra pseudo-header named "x-stream-meta" in chunk preambles. In some cases the header value contains an unescaped CRLF sequence when a per-request metadata blob is large (>512 bytes).
- Our streaming parser assumes header lines end with CRLF and treats a stray CRLF in a header value as the end of that header block. Under concurrency spikes the state machine misinterprets the next chunk boundary and throws a parse exception -> connection reset. That explains the 400s and the downstream 502/521 resets once the worker thread pool gets saturated leading to P95 latency spikes.

Root cause hypothesis: client SDK introduced a change in v2.3.1 that added the raw metadata header without length-escaping when metadata crosses payload boundaries. Parser is strict about header line framing which is by design to avoid ambiguous boundary parsing.

Immediate mitigations we can do (order matters):
1) Customer-visible workaround: instruct Acme to set SDK config REDWOOD_DISABLE_STREAMING=true OR set streamingMode: "buffered" in their SDK to avoid streaming frames. This is a 1–2 minute config flip on their side.
2) Ingress mitigation: deploy a header-sanitizer filter that strips CR/LF from incoming header values for the x-stream-meta header. This is a quick filter we can push to the ingress LB and canary in 2 hours. Risks: may drop some metadata but preserves connection stability.
3) Short-term revert: patch client SDK to escape CRLF in metadata or to base64-encode the header. We can prepare a patch and coordinate with SDK owners; rolling a client update will take longer (days) for customers to adopt.
4) Runtime hardening: make parser tolerant to quoted header values with embedded CRLF when content-length style framing present — bigger change, needs QA, target next minor release.

Action items / timeline:
- I will open a hotfix branch for the ingress sanitizer now and target a canary rollout to a subset of our frontends within ~3–4 hours. (branch: fix/header-sanitize/7421)
- Monica, please confirm whether Acme can flip REDWOOD_DISABLE_STREAMING today; if so we ask them to keep it off until we validate the ingress fix.
- Jasmine, can you ask for an executive contact at Acme in case they escalate?

Attaching: patch-headers-fix.diff (ingress sanitizer prototype)

-Karthik
Principal Software Engineer, Serving Runtime
